ra: Pachomius is a founding figure of Egyptian desert monasticism, counted among the desert fathers.
Macarius the Great is a leading abba of Scetis in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Evagrius Ponticus was a monk of Nitria/Kellia and systematizer of desert ascetic teaching.
John Cassian lived among and transmitted the teaching of the Egyptian desert fathers.
Moses the Black was an abba of Scetis represented in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Poemen is the most quoted abba in the alphabetical Apophthegmata Patrum.
Arsenius the Great was an abba of Scetis in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Paul of Thebes is traditionally the first Christian desert hermit.
Amma Syncletica is one of the desert mothers in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Amma Sarah is one of the three women in the alphabetical Apophthegmata Patrum.
Amma Theodora is one of the desert mothers in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Pambo was an abba of Nitria in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Sisoes was a desert abba who dwelt on Anthony's mountain, attested in the Apophthegmata Patrum.
Anthony the Great (existing ENT_SAINT_ANTHONY_ABBOT), the father of monasticism, is the foremost of the desert fathers; cross-link, not duplicated.
The desert fathers and mothers collectively embody and originate Christian monasticism (existing ENT_MONASTICISM, a Ritual/social category — not a deity).
The desert fathers withdrew to and dwelt in the Egyptian/Palestinian desert (existing ENT_DESERT, a Place/environment category).
Pachomius founded cenobitic (communal) monasticism, a core form of Christian monasticism (existing ENT_MONASTICISM, a Ritual/social category — not a deity).
Tradition and the Apophthegmata present Macarius the Great as a disciple of Anthony the Great (existing ENT_SAINT_ANTHONY_ABBOT).
Evagrius Ponticus was a disciple of Macarius the Great (and Macarius of Alexandria) at the Kellia/Nitria.
John Cassian transmitted Evagrian ascetic teaching, notably the eight thoughts, to Latin monasticism through his Institutes and Conferences.
Sisoes settled on Anthony the Great's inner mountain after Anthony's death, presenting himself as heir to Anthony's ascetic place and tradition.
Pambo of Nitria is associated with the Macarian circle of Nitria/Kellia in the Apophthegmata tradition.
Cassian transmitted Evagrian doctrine but tacitly distanced it from the Evagrian-Origenist speculation later condemned; a guarded reception rather than full endorsement.
